title: Two cards gone before the next draw
deckReference: Michael Loconto — Pro Tour New York 1996
era: 1996 Pro Tour New York-era Standard under current milling terminology
story: On my opponent's end step, I tapped two Island s to pay for Millstone , then tapped the artifact and targeted my opponent. They had two cards left in their library. Both cards went to the graveyard, and their hand did not change. I still had Counterspell for a possible answer, but the opponent did not lose just because their library was empty. On their next draw step, if nothing replaced or prevented the empty-library draw, they would lose while trying to draw. Millstone had created that problem without dealing a point of damage.
review: {2} paid by two Islands. Millstone itself taps and mills exactly two from a 2-card opponent library. Empty library does not immediately cause a loss; player loses on attempted draw. Exact match fictional.
